studies_head.author: Panzarella et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2024, Application of Targeted Optical Coherence Tomography in Oral Cancer- A Cross-Sectional Preliminary Study, Diagnostics.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Consecutively recruited adults at the Oral Medicine Unit, University Hospital 'Policlinico Paolo Giaccone', Palermo, Italy, January-March 2024.
studies_head.unit_of_analysis_primary: Selected-image / lesion-level (10 representative OCT scans per lesion per session)
studies_head.population_characteristics: 21 adults; mean ages by lesion subgroup: OL buccal 68.7y, OL ventral tongue 69.5y, OLP buccal 64.5y, OLP dorsal tongue 61.3y, OSCC alveolar mucosa 70.7y, OSCC lateral tongue 75.0y.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 7 OL + 7 OLP + 7 OSCC; 2520 scans per session, 210 selected images per session used for evaluation.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Target conditions were OL, OLP, and OSCC; site-coded by NIH/SEER ICD-O-3.2 oral topography codes. One-vs-rest diagnostic assessment reported for each lesion type.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: VivoSight SS-OCT (Michelson Diagnostics), swept-source Fourier-domain OCT; 1305 ± 15 nm, >=150 nm sweep range, axial <10 um, lateral <7.5 um, 6x6 mm scan, 120 slices, 50 um slice step, 12 s scan.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: Clinician pattern-based OCT interpretation by 2 blinded observers; pre-target and post-target site registration sessions.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Targeted punch biopsy / histopathology on the pre-registered site; FFPE 5 um H&E sections; blinded pathologist; biopsy after OCT registration workflow.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: High / explicit targeted co-registration using punch-site marking, photographs, sutures, and diametral specimen marking.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: No numeric classifier threshold; diagnosis based on predefined structured OCT pattern criteria for OL, OLP, OSCC.
studies_head.internal_vs_external_validation_for_AI: Not applicable (no AI model validation in this paper)
studies_head.vendor_involvement: No explicit vendor involvement beyond device manufacturer naming
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Exploratory / subgroup evidence only; not a clean primary patient-level DTA study because selected scans per lesion were analyzed.
studies_head.notes: Strong procedural standardization; very useful for biopsy-site matching and protocol development.

studies_head.author: Yuan et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2022, Noninvasive oral cancer screening based on local residual adaptation network using optical coherence tomography, MBEC.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Patients treated at Beijing Stomatological Hospital, Capital Medical University, China, Sept 2020-Feb 2021; images collected immediately after surgery resection.
studies_head.prospective_or_retrospective: Prospective sample collection with train/test image split
studies_head.unit_of_analysis_primary: Image-level (2-D images released from 3-D OCT volumes)
studies_head.population_characteristics: 25 patients; 264 3-D OCT images -> 26,400 2-D images total. Training set 13,900 images, testing set 12,500 images.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 120 non-cancerous and 144 cancerous 3-D OCT images; tissues from tongue, floor of mouth, upper/lower gingiva, buccal mucosa, cheek pouch, oropharynx; non-cancerous vs cancerous binary task.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Binary target condition: cancerous vs non-cancerous oral tissue in ex vivo OCT images.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Homemade ultra-high-resolution OCT microscopy system; 300 nm spectral bandwidth, 800 nm center wavelength, axial 1.5 um in tissue, lateral 3.5 um, ~2 mm penetration depth.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: AI / deep learning classifiers: VGG-16, GoogLeNet, Inception-V3, ResNet-50, GRAN-50, LRAN-18, LRAN-34, LRAN-50.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Pathologist-annotated labels from surgical specimens; tissue imaged immediately after resection. Histopathology/pathologist ground truth implied but exact one-to-one biopsy-site timing/co-registration not fully detailed.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate / unclear at exact site level; pathology supervision present but explicit same-site histology mapping is limited in the extracted text.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: No clinical threshold. Model outputs from deep-learning classifiers; LRAN described with cross-entropy plus local adaptation.
studies_head.internal_vs_external_validation_for_AI: Internal train/test split only; no explicit external validation reported.
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Qualitative / exploratory or AI subgroup evidence; not suitable for primary in-vivo patient-level meta-analysis.
studies_head.notes: Excellent source for model-level confusion matrices, but ex vivo image-level design limits direct compatibility with the updated review's primary analysis.

studies_head.author: James et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2021, Validation of a Point-of-Care Optical Coherence Tomography Device with Machine Learning Algorithm for Detection of Oral Potentially Malignant and Malignant Lesions, Cancers.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Tertiary cancer center, dental oral medicine clinic, and community screening camps across Bangalore, India, Dec 2015-Nov 2016.
studies_head.unit_of_analysis_primary: Sub-site / image-level and site-level model outputs
studies_head.population_characteristics: Adults >18 years with oral lesions; exclusions included mouth opening <2 cm, TB/HIV/HBV/HCV treatment, oral cancer treatment, pregnancy.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 249 recruited subjects; 381 sub-sites captured, 347 sub-sites analyzed; lesion groups benign/normal n=151, OPML n=121, malignant n=75 (per abstract/lesion counts).
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Target conditions include OSCC vs dysplasia/benign/normal; dysplasia vs benign/normal; and high-grade dysplasia vs low-grade dysplasia/benign/normal.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Portable spectral-domain OCT with 2D scanning long GRIN rod probe; 930 nm center wavelength, axial 7 um, lateral 15 um, penetration 0.2-1 mm, imaging speed 1.2 kHz.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: Automated non-deep-learning algorithm-score and AI/ML ANN-SVM models (DenseNet-201-SVM, Inception-ResNet-v2-SVM; 14 ANN feature extractors explored).
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathology for biopsied lesions, but clinical diagnosis used where biopsy was not indicated; imaging followed by biopsy within 10-15 min when biopsied.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate / partial: same lesion site for biopsied lesions, but some normal/benign lesions used clinical diagnosis instead of pathology.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Algorithm-score thresholds prespecified: malignant -0.0580 to -0.0780; dysplastic -0.0780 to -0.0918; normal -0.0918 to -0.1280. ANN-SVM thresholds from ROC in cross-validation set.
studies_head.internal_vs_external_validation_for_AI: Internal training / cross-validation / independent stand-alone test set; no explicit external validation.
studies_head.vendor_involvement: No explicit vendor involvement; portable low-cost OCT developed by study group
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Potentially usable in secondary/meta-regression subgroup analyses, but not ideal for primary histopathology-only binary meta-analysis because some benign/normal labels were clinical rather than histologic.
studies_head.notes: Important study because it directly spans clinician-style algorithm and ANN-based interpretation pathways in vivo.

studies_head.author: Ridgway et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2006, In Vivo Optical Coherence Tomography of the human oral cavity and oropharynx, Arch Otolaryngo Head and Neck surgery.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: University of California Irvine outpatient clinic and operative endoscopy; adults imaged during oral examination/endoscopy.
studies_head.unit_of_analysis_primary: Patient-level with multiple imaged sites; no formal DTA primary unit
studies_head.population_characteristics: 41 adults aged 24–89 years; operative endoscopy in 34 and outpatient clinic in 7.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: Normal healthy tissues, benign pathologic features, premalignant lesions, invasive cancer, transition zones across oral cavity and oropharynx.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Descriptive characterization of oral cavity/oropharyngeal mucosa and pathology, not a single binary diagnostic target.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Custom fiber-based OCT; 1310 nm source, axial ~10 µm/pixel, lateral ~10 µm/pixel, handheld flexible probe, 1.6 mm depth.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Biopsy when clinically indicated, otherwise comparison with standard histologic criteria.
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Background / qualitative only; not poolable for DTA meta-analysis
studies_head.notes: Important foundational in vivo oral OCT paper but not a formal diagnostic-accuracy study.

studies_head.author: Tsai et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2008, Effective indicators for diagnosis of oral cancer using optical coherence tomography, Optics Express.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: National Taiwan University Hospital clinical buccal mucosa scanning with biopsy of lesion sites; nearby normal mucosa scanned as controls.
studies_head.population_characteristics: 32 patients aged 30–77 years; 84 samples total from buccal mucosa.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 35 normal controls, 16 epithelial hyperplasia, 18 moderate dysplasia, 15 SCC.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Multiple binary targets reported: MD/SCC vs normal; EH/MD vs normal; indicator-specific analyses.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Portable swept-source OCT; 1310 nm, sensitivity 103 dB, axial 8 µm free space, lateral 15 µm, handheld probe.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathology for lesion sites; normal controls nearby without biopsy.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate / biopsy within 5 mm unit but not exact same-site for controls
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Prespecified indicator thresholds (e.g., SD 0.12, α 0.078–0.079 µm, T 300 µm).
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Secondary / subgroup evidence; scan-level and threshold-sweep design
studies_head.notes: Useful older quantitative OCT study; direct pooling should be cautious because controls were not biopsied and multiple threshold families were tested.

studies_head.author: Wilder-Smith et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2009, In Vivo Diagnosis of Oral Dysplasia and Malignancy Using Optical Coherence Tomography- Preliminary Studies in 50 Patients, Lasers Surg Med.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Patients with suspect oral leukoplakia/erythroplakia at UCI Department of Otolaryngology and UCLA Oral Medicine Clinic.
studies_head.population_characteristics: 50 patients with healthy, dysplastic, or malignant lesions included after exclusions.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: Healthy, dysplastic, carcinoma in situ, and SCC lesions.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Binary targets include carcinoma in situ or SCC vs non-cancer and SCC vs all other pathologies.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Fiberoptic high-resolution 3D OCT probe or Niris 2D probe, in-depth resolution 10–15 µm.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: Clinician-read OCT by two blinded pre-trained scorers
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Biopsy and routine histopathology for each lesion after OCT imaging.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate / lesion-centered but exact histology plane matching limited
studies_head.vendor_involvement: Loan of Niris system by Imalux acknowledged
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Potentially poolable for in vivo clinician-read subgroup
studies_head.notes: Strong classic human in vivo DTA paper; some direct counts are only partially recoverable from summary text.

studies_head.author: Lee et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2012, Diagnosis of oral precancer with optical coherence tomography, Biometical optics express.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Clinical scanning at National Taiwan University Hospital during patient visits; buccal mucosa OCT with paired lesion and nearby normal site.
studies_head.study_design: Prospective OCT image-analysis / diagnostic statistics study
studies_head.population_characteristics: 54 patients; 137 buccal mucosa OCT images from 54 patients.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 54 normal, 39 mild dysplasia, 44 moderate dysplasia images.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Primary emphasis on differentiating moderate dysplasia from mild dysplasia and from normal.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Swept-source OCT 1310 nm; 103 dB sensitivity; 6 µm axial resolution in tissue; 7 µm lateral resolution.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: Automated non-deep-learning OCT image analysis (SD mapping)
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathology from biopsy; OCT location cannot be exactly the same as biopsy location.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate / imperfect same-site correlation explicitly acknowledged
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Secondary / subgroup evidence only; image-level and precancer-focused
studies_head.notes: Important for OPMD stratification but not ideal for main binary cancer-vs-noncancer pooling.

studies_head.author: Hamdoon et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2013, Optical coherence tomography in the assessment of suspicious oral lesions, an immediate ex vivo study, Photodiagnosis and photodynamic therapy.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: 125 consecutive suspicious oral lesions at UCL Head and Neck Centre, London; biopsied lesions scanned in immediate ex vivo phase.
studies_head.study_design: Prospective immediate ex vivo clinical study
studies_head.population_characteristics: 125 patients with suspicious oral lesions; lesions >1 cm included.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 43 microinvasive carcinomas, 41 dysplasias, 22 keratoses, 11 non-specific lesions, 6 mucoceles, 2 papillomas.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Potentially malignant/malignant disorders requiring biopsy vs benign/non-specific lesions; also reader-level differential diagnosis.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Michelson Diagnostics EX1301 swept-source frequency-domain OCT microscope; 1310 nm, axial <10 µm, lateral <10 µm, 6 mm width, 1.5 mm depth.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: Clinician and pathologist structured OCT reading
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathology of same biopsy specimen after OCT scanning.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Structured OCT reading score / need-for-biopsy decision.
studies_head.notes: Good same-specimen pathology matching, but ex vivo design and “future need for biopsy” framing differ from pure in vivo screening studies.

studies_head.author: Heidari et al.

studies_head.file_name: 2018, Optical Coherence Tomography as an Oral Cancer Screening Adjunct in a Low Resource Setting, IEEE JSTQE.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Mazumdar Shaw Cancer Center, Bangalore, India; pilot low-resource screening study with healthy volunteers and suspicious lesions.
studies_head.unit_of_analysis_primary: Subject-level and image-level (2D B-scans by site)
studies_head.population_characteristics: 30 subjects total: 20 with suspicious oral lesions and 10 healthy subjects.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 10 normal, 5 mild dysplasia, 3 moderate dysplasia, 2 severe dysplasia, 10 OSCC.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Binary tasks healthy vs dysplasia/cancer and cancer vs dysplasia; intended triage / screening use.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Portable SD-OCT with long GRIN rod probe; 930 nm, axial 7 µm, lateral 15 µm.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: Clinician visual scorer and automated non-deep-learning algorithm
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Algorithm used peak-count and basement-membrane deviation criteria.
studies_head.vendor_involvement: Custom system by UC Irvine collaborators
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Potentially poolable for secondary in vivo subgroup
studies_head.notes: Small pilot but clinically relevant low-resource screening adjunct study.

studies_head.author: Jerjes et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2019, Epithelial tissue thickness improves optical coherence tomography’s ability in detecting oral cancer, Photodiagnosis and photodynamic therapy.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Immediate ex vivo prospective study of resected OSCC margins from T1/T2 N0 patients at UCL.
studies_head.study_design: Immediate ex vivo prospective validation / reproducibility study
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: 189 cancer-free margins and 51 cancer-involved margins across eight oral anatomical sites.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Cancer-involved vs cancer-free margins; thickness-only and combined architectural+thickness analyses.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Michelson Diagnostics EX1301 OCT microscope; 1310 nm, axial <10 µm, lateral <10 µm, 6 mm width, 1.5 mm depth.
studies_head.interpretation_pathway_category: Clinician/structural OCT interpretation plus epithelial thickness measurement
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathology of co-localized resection margins; repeated OCT at immediate, 1 h saline, 24 h formalin.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: High for ex vivo margin specimens with co-registration
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Combined safe/risk epithelial thickness units plus architectural changes.
studies_head.vendor_involvement: Competing interest with Michelson Diagnostics reported
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Separate ex vivo margin subgroup only
studies_head.notes: Very useful for margin use-case, not for main in vivo lesion diagnosis meta-analysis.

studies_head.author: Sunny et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2019, Intra-operative point-of-procedure delineation of oral cancer margins using optical coherence tomography, oral oncology.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bangalore, India; intraoperative imaging during OSCC surgery.
studies_head.population_characteristics: 14 adults with newly diagnosed OSCC; 125 images captured, 120 analyzable.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: SCC, mild/moderate/severe dysplasia, and non-dysplastic lesions across tumor, tumor margin, surgical margin, >1 cm margin, contralateral mucosa.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Malignant field delineation and dysplastic field delineation around tumor margins.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Portable SD-OCT with 1-D scanning probe; 930 nm, axial 7 µm, lateral 15 µm, 2 images/s; algorithmic neoplastic score.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Punch biopsies from each imaged site with blinded WHO-based histopathology.
studies_head.funding_source: Department of Bio-Technology India and NIH
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Potentially poolable in site-level in vivo subgroup
studies_head.notes: Excellent for field-cancerization and intraoperative mapping; site-level rather than patient-level.

studies_head.author: Obade et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2021, Application of optical coherence tomography to study the structural features of oral mucosa in biopsy tissues of oral dysplasia and carcinomas, Clin Oral Investig.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Oral surgery clinic, University of Malaya; biopsies scanned in laboratory within 1 hour.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: OSCC (15 samples), epithelial dysplasia (7), benign lesions and normal mucosa (30).
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Differentiating benign disorders, dysplasia, and OSCC based on OCT structural features of biopsy tissues.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Swept-source OCT (Thorlabs OCS1300SS), 1325 nm; individual scan 10 mm wide.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathology of same biopsy tissue after formalin fixation.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: High for specimen-level, but ex vivo
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Structured five-variable OCT scoring; no binary threshold.
studies_head.notes: Good observer agreement study, but not a direct pooled DTA paper with standard 2×2 outputs.

studies_head.author: Yang et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2021, Identification of oral precancerous and cancerous tissue by swept source optical coherence, Lasers Surg Med.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Tianjin Stomatological Hospital; fresh ex vivo tissues imaged intraoperatively after resection.
studies_head.study_design: Ex vivo machine-learning tissue classification study
studies_head.prospective_or_retrospective: Prospective sample collection with internal train/test split
studies_head.population_characteristics: 19 patients (14 OSCC, 5 LEH) plus 14 normal areas; 71 sites and 5176 images.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Three-class identification of normal mucosa vs LEH vs OSCC in ex vivo OCT images.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Homemade SS-OCT with 100 kHz swept source; axial ~14 µm in air, lateral 17 µm, 6×6 mm2 field, 100 fps.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathology-confirmed tissue type under surgeon/pathologist guidance.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: ANN multiclass classifier after PCA; attenuation-model thresholds secondary.
studies_head.funding_source: National Natural Science Foundation of China and local grants
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: AI subgroup / qualitative for current review
studies_head.notes: Strong engineering paper with direct multiclass confusion matrix; ex vivo and LEH-focused.

studies_head.author: Heidari et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2021, The Use of Optical Coherence Tomography and Convolutional Neural Networks to Distinguish normal and abnormal oral mucosa, Journal Biophotonics.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Prospectively enrolled patients undergoing composite resection of head and neck squamous lesions at University of California Irvine Medical Center; fresh resected specimens transported to pathology and oriented by the surgeon for OCT imaging of margins and transition zones.
studies_head.in_vivo_or_ex_vivo: Ex vivo / fresh resected specimen imaging
studies_head.unit_of_analysis_primary: 3-D OCT volume-level for primary CNN classification; B-scan level used within volumes
studies_head.population_characteristics: Seven patients in methods/table (5 male, 2 female) with six squamous cell carcinoma and one squamous dysplasia; cancer locations included tongue, tonsil, soft palate, floor of mouth, lower lip, buccal mucosa; abstract/front matter inconsistently mentions nine patients.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: Head and neck/oral mucosal margins; normal/abnormal classification across fresh resected mucosa, including SCC and dysplasia versus healthy tissue.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Fresh resected head and neck mucosal specimens and tissue margins; target condition was abnormal tissue (cancer/dysplasia) versus normal on margin evaluation.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: VCSEL swept-source OCT with microscope scanning probe; 1310 nm center wavelength, 100 nm bandwidth, 200 kHz laser, real-time GPU processing; 7x7 mm 3-D volumes with 1000 B-scans, acquired in ~7 s per volume.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Permanent histopathology / pathology report from co-registered specimen regions; surgeon orientation, digital video and audio dictation used to aid co-registration; single histologic section per imaged volume.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate; co-registration at specimen-region level but not each B-scan, and authors explicitly note finer section-to-section histologic labels were not attainable.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Volumetric normal vs abnormal classification by majority probability from CNN output; no externally prespecified clinical threshold.
studies_head.internal_vs_external_validation_for_AI: Internal validation only (transfer learning with train/validation split); no external validation.
studies_head.vendor_involvement: Potential competing interest: Zhongping Chen has financial interests with OCT Medical Inc., but work not supported by company.
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Exploratory / subgroup evidence only; not suitable for primary oral in-vivo patient-level DTA pooling.
studies_head.notes: Important missing study if total should be 14. Head-and-neck margin study rather than pure oral lesion diagnostic cohort; accuracy metrics available but confusion counts are not directly reported in extractable form.

studies_head.author: Hamdoon et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2016, Optical coherence tomography in the assessment of oral squamous cell carcinoma resection margins, Photodiagnosis and photodynamic therapy.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: 28 consecutive T1-T2 N0M0 OSCC patients at the UCLH Head and Neck Centre, London, recruited 2008-2010 for immediate ex vivo margin assessment after tumor resection.
studies_head.study_design: Prospective immediate ex vivo margin-assessment study
studies_head.population_characteristics: 28 patients; mean age 61 years (range 36-103); 19 male/9 female; T1-T2 N0 OSCC only.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: OSCC resection margins only; 90 tumor-free margins and 22 tumor-involved margins.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Ventro-lateral tongue, floor of mouth, retromolar trigone, buccal mucosa and other oral cavity sites; target condition = tumor-involved surgical margin vs tumor-free margin.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Michelson Diagnostics EX1301 swept-source frequency-domain OCT microscope; 1310 nm imaging wavelength; axial <10 µm, lateral <10 µm, max width 6 mm, imaging depth 1.5 mm; specimens scanned within 1 hour of resection in saline.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histopathologic assessment of all four surgical margins for each specimen by one oral and maxillofacial pathologist after immediate ex vivo OCT scanning.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: High for specimen-margin level; co-registration used diagrams, digital images, sutures and special ink.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: No numeric threshold; structured visual criteria based on architectural changes, epithelial thickness and basement membrane breach.
studies_head.funding_source: Not specifically reported in extracted text.
studies_head.vendor_involvement: Yes; Colin Hopper advisory board member and Gordon McKenzie medical applications director at Michelson Diagnostics.
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Secondary / ex vivo margin subgroup evidence
studies_head.notes: Useful margin-assessment study with direct 2x2 tables for two readers; not primary in vivo lesion-detection design.

studies_head.author: Yang et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2020, Identification of oral cancer in OCT images based on an optical attenuation model, Lasers in Medical Science.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Fresh oral tissues obtained from Tianjin Stomatological Hospital, Tianjin, China; ex vivo tissues from 14 OSCC patients scanned immediately after surgery resection.
studies_head.study_design: Ex vivo quantitative threshold-development and validation study
studies_head.prospective_or_retrospective: Prospective sample collection with internal validation split
studies_head.population_characteristics: 14 patients with OSCC; validation dataset 638 images (322 cancer, 316 non-cancer), training dataset 3174 images.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: Cancerous versus non-cancerous oral tissues from gingiva and tongue predominately; fresh ex vivo tissues.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Target condition = OSCC tissue versus non-cancer tissue in excised oral specimens.
studies_head.OCT_device_platform_and_scan_protocol: Portable home-made swept-source OCT; central wavelength 1310 nm, 100 kHz sweep rate, axial resolution 14 µm in air, lateral 17 µm; 2D images 1024x1000 pixels and 3D datasets of 1000 B-scans.
studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Histology after OCT scanning; specialized pathologist independently assessed whether slices contained cancerous tissue and generated final pathological reports.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate; histology slides digitized and corresponding to OCT images, but exact site-registration workflow not fully detailed.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: Optical attenuation threshold 4.7 mm^-1 selected from training data as maximum sensitivity with at least 80% specificity.
studies_head.funding_source: National Natural Science Foundation of China, Tianjin Science and Technology Support Program, and Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities.
studies_head.study_design_fit_to_current_review: Exploratory / ex vivo AI-quantitative subgroup evidence
studies_head.notes: Quantitative attenuation-threshold paper; good sensitivity/specificity but image-level ex vivo design.

studies_head.author: Yang et al.
studies_head.file_name: 2023, Deep-Learning-Based Automated Identification and Visualization of Oral Cancer in Optical Coherence Tomography Images, Biomedicines.pdf
studies_head.clinical_setting_and_recruitment_method: Fresh tissue samples from Tianjin Stomatology Hospital, China; 19 patients with oral diseases (LEH and OSCC) with normal mucosa captured from abnormal excisions.
studies_head.study_design: Ex vivo multi-class AI classification study
studies_head.prospective_or_retrospective: Prospective tissue collection with train/test split
studies_head.population_characteristics: 19 patients total (5 LEH, 14 OSCC; normal mucosa from abnormal excised tissues). Total dataset 13,799 ROI images; test set 4,062 ROI images.
studies_head.lesion_spectrum: Normal mucosa, leukoplakia with hyperplasia (LEH), and OSCC.
studies_head.lesion_site_and_target_condition_definit: Three-class identification of normal mucosa vs LEH vs OSCC from ex vivo OCT images; normal area at least 1 cm away from abnormal area.

studies_head.reference_standard_method_and_timing: Tissues scanned then fixed and H&E stained; slices evaluated by experienced pathologist and OCT images matched with histopathologic images.
studies_head.biopsy_site_matching_quality: Moderate to high; ROI images matched with histopathologic images after tissue scanning.
studies_head.threshold_definition_if_applicable: No clinical threshold; classification by CNN outputs / one-vs-rest multiclass metrics.
studies_head.internal_vs_external_validation_for_AI: Internal train/test split with 10-fold cross-validation; no external validation.
studies_head.funding_source: National Natural Science Foundation of China, Tianjin Science and Technology Support Program, Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Basic Research Cooperation Special Program.

studies_head.study_design: Ex vivo AI diagnostic validation study with image-level and resected patch-level evaluation

rows.TITLE: ABSTRACT
rows.Accurate and timely intraoperative class: Precise and timely intraoperative classification of vocal cord leukoplakia is vital for early staging and detection of laryngeal cancer. Current endoscopic imaging, such as narrow-band imaging (NBI) and white-light laryngoscopy (WLI), has the capability to evaluate the malignancy, but has low sensitivity (<70%) for grading the low-risk dysplasia. For the vocal fold lesions, optical coherence tomography (OCT), a non-invasive imaging technology, has been widely used to show the texture and pixel change of lesions caused by squamous epithelial cell hyperplasia and atypical hyperplasia. Here, a handheld OCT probe (OD = 3 mm, length = 25 cm) was designed and fabricated, and a swept-source OCT system was built for vocal lesion monitoring during the surgery. Home-built OCT probe has both a small OD and a long length for penetration depth imaging with good quality, which may enable the accurate and timely intraoperative localization detection of vocal cord tissues. The probe system has a 2D imaging speed of 100 frames per second, 7.96 µm lateral resolution, 16.24 µm axial resolution, and an imaging depth of 2.12 ± 0.43 mm in vocal fold tissues. We collected 378 OCT b-scan images (114 low risk, 175 high risk, 89 malignant) from 12 patients (4 low risk, five high risk, three malignant). A total of eight features of single B-scan images were extracted, including the mean pixel intensity (PI), median PI, minimum PI, and maximum PI; meanwhile, the mean attenuation coefficient (AC), median AC, minimum AC, and maximum AC of A-lines. The random forest (RF) model achieved the best overall accuracy (92.59%) and recall (93.25%) for low risk, high risk, and malignant classification, using 5-fold validation, with each patient’s assessment completed within 10 minutes. Our OCT system was demonstrated to provide rapid and accurate pathological diagnosis of vocal cord leukoplakia intraoperatively. Our handheld OCT system facilitates identification of low-risk dysplasia with a sensitivity of up to 84.21% during the surgery, offering critical guidance on whether to opt for conservative or surgical treatment based on the lesion’s severity.

rows.Accurate and timely intraoperative class: Purpose : Handheld optical coherence tomography (OCT) has enabled studies of early human foveal development in preterm infants. Macular edema (ME) at 32 +/- 1 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) appears protective against development of treatment-requiring retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) and an “indeterminate fovea” (IF) represents a risk factor for future severe ROP. However, systemic factors affecting early human foveal development remains unknown. We hypothesize that an IF is associated with younger gestational age (GA), lower birth weight (BW), and systemic neonatal risk factors. Methods : We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 299 eyes (157 infants) in an OCT database with OCT imaging at 32 ± 1 weeks PMA. Eyes were manually categorized as “established fovea”, “IF”, and “ME”. OCT measurements, demographics, and clinical characteristics (e.g. sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), periventricular leukomalacia (PVL), patent ductus arteriosus (PDA), bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD)) were extracted. Univariable and multivariable regression models were used to evaluate the association between ME and IF at 32 ± 1 weeks PMA and systemic risk factors. Results : Among 157 infants, 75 had an established fovea, 43 had an IF, and 39 had ME. All foveal categorizations were consistent bilaterally. Indeterminate fovea was associated with lower GA in univariable (p < 0.001) and multivariable analyses (p < 0.001). Lower BW showed significance in univariable analysis but was not significant after adjusting for GA and race. PDA demonstrated a significant association with IF in both univariable (p < 0.001) and multivariable analyses (p = 0.009). Combined sepsis and NEC, and combined IVH and PVL, were significant in univariable analysis but did not maintain significance in multivariable models. ME was similarly associated with lower GA in both univariate (p = 0.008) and multivariate analyses (p = 0.003). It was also linked to lower BW in multivariable analysis (p = 0.041). Conclusions : IF and ME at 32 ± 1 weeks PMA are both associated with lower GA, with ME additionally associated with lower BW. PDA may represent a risk factor associated with poorer foveal development. (Table Presented).

rows.TITLE: ABSTRACT
rows.Accurate and timely intraoperative class: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is promising to become an essential imaging tool for non-invasive oral mucosal tissue assessment, but it faces challenges like speckle noise and motion artifacts. In addition, it is difficult to distinguish different layers of oral mucosal tissues from gray level OCT images due to the similarity of optical properties between different layers. We introduce the Efficient Segmentation-Denoising Model (ESDM), a multi-task deep learning framework designed to enhance OCT imaging by reducing scan time from ∼8s to ∼2s and improving oral epithelium layer segmentation. ESDM also presents high accuracy in quantifying oral epithelium thickness, achieving mean absolute errors as low as 5 µm compared to manual measurements. This research shows that ESDM can notably improve OCT imaging and reduce the cost of accurate oral epithermal segmentation, improving diagnostic capabilities in clinical settings.

rows.TITLE: ABSTRACT
rows.Accurate and timely intraoperative class: Background: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is an advanced imaging technique that is widely used in ophthalmology and is increasingly being applied in other fields of medicine. In oral oncology, OCT offers high-resolution, non-invasive (uses non-ionizing light), label-free, real-time imaging, providing detailed insights into tissue microanatomy and cellular structures, thus having the potential to improve early detection, monitoring and cost-effective screening of high-risk populations. However, significant challenges remain in applying OCT to OSCC and OPMDs, particularly in clinical practice. Methods: A comprehensive search of PUBMED, SCOPUS, and Web of Science databases was performed up to October 2024. Additional manual searches were conducted by screening article bibliographies. Inclusion criteria encompassed studies published in English involving human subjects and evaluating the role of OCT in OSCC and OPMD assessment, OCT utilization for margin resection, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted interpretation of OCT images. After removal of duplicates and screening of titles and abstracts, full-text analysis was conducted on eligible studies. Results: The technique has been investigated for its accuracy in identifying malignant changes in tissues before surgery and/or evaluating resection margins during surgery. Although early studies, primarily in animal models, have been extended to humans and have demonstrated the potential of OCT to accurately assess resection margins and identify precancerous lesions, significant limitations persist. The high cost of OCT equipment reduces its accessibility, availability and widespread use as a common investigation methodology in non-experimental settings. In addition, there is significant heterogeneity in the methodologies used to interpret OCT data, which is strictly operator dependent and may affect standardization and reproducibility of results. This is further complicated by the introduction and increased trend to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms in imaging evaluation. Machine learning and deep learning algorithms have shown superior diagnostic sensitivity and accuracy compared to clinician judgment. However, especially when used to assess resection margins, these algorithms may be significantly affected by sample extension and preparation, which remains a barrier to the routine clinical application of OCT systems. Conclusion: Addressing the advantages and challenges of this emerging technique may help focus future research on standardizing application protocols and enhancing AI-assisted analysis to improve diagnostic performance and facilitate clinical translation.
